edges.parent_basis:
THE ONE CROSS-LINE EDGE IN THIS RECORD, and it is drawn because the act draws
it. At its second sentence the constitution turns back to 25 January 1959 and
records that on that day John XXIII first publicly announced his decision to
reform the body of canon law then in force, `which had been promulgated in the
year 1917 at the solemnity of Pentecost`; two paragraphs later it asks why John
XXIII felt the necessity of reforming the Code then in force and answers that
the reform was demanded by the Council. An act that says what it revises has
drawn its own edge. [read at lines 46 and 48 of the extracted text of the Latin
delivery named in `citation`.]

The effect is stronger than a descent. The 1983 Code's own canon 6 §1 1°
ABROGATES the Code of 1917 outright, and this repository has already verified
that canon against the Vatican's Latin delivery [passage.catholic-church.codex-
iuris-canonici-1983.latin-vatican-web-codex-2026-07-25.canon-6, states
cataloged/acquired/inspected/verified]. So the departures this station carries
are not a revision of the 1917 canons but the removal of every one of them, and
the arrival of a Code numbered independently.
